correctness.rationale: For the explicitly encoded graph exhaustive enumeration reconstructs all 126 nonempty faces and all 12 deletion/link pairs. The actual checker constructs acyclic element matchings on whole (62 pairs, crit 0+2), deletion A (49, crit 0), deletion B (48, crit 0+2), link A (12, crit 0+1) and link B (13, crit 0), verifying every directed incidence by full topological sort. It also actually constructs valid free-face collapse orders for deletion A and link B, verifies two automorphism generators and orbit separation by 99 versus 98 deletion face counts, and proves all vertex deletions decrease chromatic number from 4 to 3. Discrete Morse CW theorem implies S^2/S^1 as stated; gluing the cone on contractible links makes canonical deletion inclusions homotopy equivalences in orbit B. Independent full F2 boundary-rank calculations on all 12 deletions/links corroborate homology, but are not substituted for homotopy proof.

value.rationale: The Chvátal graph is a canonical smallest triangle-free 4-regular 4-chromatic graph. A complete finite automorphism-orbit classification of its 12 vertex links/deletions is naturally motivated, not an arbitrary choice of a numerical slice. The theorem exhibits a real structural distinction: all vertices are chromatically critical, but exactly four are homotopy-critical; the other eight have homotopy-equivalent canonical deletion inclusions. Actual simplicial collapsibility certificates strengthen a mere Betti-count observation, while modest finite scope is stated explicitly.
